summary: This second lecture goes back to introduce three key figures in the Prophet's family: Hashim, Abdul Muttalib and Abdullah. The ustaz explains how Hashim (whose real name was Amr) served soup and bread to the pilgrims, married Salma in Yathrib and died in Gaza. His son Shaibah grew up in Yathrib until his uncle Al-Muttalib brought him to Mecca, where he was called Abdul Muttalib. After becoming leader of the Quraysh, Abdul Muttalib rediscovered the well of zamzam through a dream, vowed to sacrifice one son if he were given ten, and finally ransomed Abdullah with a hundred camels. Abdullah married Aminah and died on the way back from Sham while Aminah was carrying the Prophet SAW.
keyPoints: According to some sirah books, the elephant army's attack came 50 days before the Prophet SAW was born.
Hashim, whose real name was Amr, was called Hashim because he crumbled bread into soup for the pilgrims.
Hashim died in Gaza, and his son Shaibah was raised in Yathrib until Al-Muttalib brought him to Mecca, where he was called Abdul Muttalib.
Abdul Muttalib rediscovered the well of zamzam through a dream that came for four nights.
He vowed to sacrifice one son if given ten, and ransomed Abdullah with a hundred camels.
Abdullah married Aminah and died on the way back from Sham while she was pregnant.

chapters.title: Opening, a prayer for Gaza and the three key figures
chapters.summary: The ustaz recalls the elephant army and says that today we go back to get to know Hashim, Abdul Muttalib and Abdullah.

chapters.title: Surah Quraysh and the blessing of food and safety
chapters.summary: The surah after Al-Fil speaks of the Quraysh's winter and summer journeys, which left them fed and safe.

chapters.title: Hashim, whose real name was Amr
chapters.summary: Hashim inherited from his father Abdul Manaf the duty of feeding the pilgrims.

chapters.title: Soup and bread for the pilgrims
chapters.summary: Hashim crumbled bread into the soup so the pilgrims would be full, which is where the name Hashim comes from.

chapters.title: Hashim, Salma and his death in Gaza
chapters.summary: On his way to Sham, Hashim married Salma in Yathrib, then fell ill and died in Gaza.

chapters.title: Shaibah is hidden in Yathrib
chapters.summary: Salma gave birth to Shaibah, who had white hair, and kept him hidden from the people of Mecca because she feared Al-Muttalib.

chapters.title: Al-Muttalib brings Shaibah to Mecca
chapters.summary: Al-Muttalib persuaded the weeping Salma to give up Shaibah, and the people of Mecca called him Abdul Muttalib.

chapters.title: Abdul Muttalib becomes leader, and how zamzam was lost
chapters.summary: After Al-Muttalib died in Yemen, Abdul Muttalib was appointed leader. Zamzam had been buried by the Jurhum Arabs hundreds of years earlier.

chapters.title: The dream that showed where zamzam was
chapters.summary: For four nights Abdul Muttalib was told in a dream to dig, and on the fourth night zamzam and its place were named.

chapters.title: Digging zamzam
chapters.summary: He dug with his sons until the old swords and armour buried by Jurhum came out.

chapters.title: The dispute over zamzam and the vow of ten sons
chapters.summary: The Arabs wanted to share zamzam, so Abdul Muttalib vowed to sacrifice a son if he were given ten sons.

chapters.title: Seeking a soothsayer, and water in the desert
chapters.summary: On the way to a soothsayer in Sham the water ran out, Allah inspired Abdul Muttalib to the place of water, and the Arabs conceded zamzam to him.

chapters.title: Ten sons and the hundred-camel ransom
chapters.summary: Abdul Muttalib was given ten sons and the youngest, Abdullah, was nearly sacrificed, but was ransomed with a hundred camels by drawing arrows.

chapters.title: Abdullah marries Aminah
chapters.summary: Abdullah became famous, married Aminah and bought a slave girl named Ummu Aiman, whom he gave to Aminah.

chapters.title: The death of Abdullah
chapters.summary: Abdullah died in Yathrib on the way back from Sham, and Ummu Aiman stayed with Aminah who was pregnant.

books.context: A summary of the sirah covering the lineage, Abdul Muttalib and the story of zamzam.

people.role: Great-grandfather of the Prophet SAW, real name Amr
people.context: Served soup and bread to the pilgrims, married Salma and died in Gaza.
Looked after the food and drink of those who came for Hajj and passed the duty to Hashim.
Gave birth to Shaibah and kept him hidden, and wept when Al-Muttalib took her son.
Brought Shaibah to Mecca, raised him, and died in Yemen.

people.role: Grandfather of the Prophet SAW and leader of the Quraysh
people.context: His birth name was Shaibah because of his white hair. He found zamzam and vowed to sacrifice a son.
Abdul Muttalib's youngest son, ransomed with a hundred camels, who married Aminah and died in Yathrib.
Abdullah's wife, who was pregnant when Abdullah died.
Bought by Abdullah at nine years old from Africa, she kept Aminah company and later cared for the Prophet SAW, who called her his mother.
Mentioned when Hajar and Ismail were left in Mecca before zamzam sprang up.
Left in Mecca with Ismail, and zamzam sprang up for them.
Left in Mecca with his mother Hajar. After he died, the Jurhum Arabs turned wicked.
Came and caused the zamzam water to spring up.

lessons.title: Be grateful for health and safety
lessons.body: The ustaz urges us to be grateful that we are healthy, fed and safe, and to pray for our brothers and sisters in Gaza who live in fear.

lessons.title: Being fed and safe are blessings from Allah
lessons.body: Surah Quraysh reminds us that feeling full and feeling safe are gifts from Allah, who protected the Kaaba without any human weapons.

lessons.title: Honouring Allah's guests
lessons.body: Hashim thought of a tastier and more filling dish for pilgrims who were tired and hungry.

lessons.title: Striving without giving up
lessons.body: When the water ran out in the desert, Abdul Muttalib refused to give up, and Allah inspired him to where there was water.

lessons.title: Allah helps those who strive
lessons.body: Allah inspired Abdul Muttalib to the place of water in the middle of the desert, until the other Arab leaders admitted that zamzam was his.

lessons.title: Do not go to soothsayers
lessons.body: The ustaz stresses that we must not believe in soothsayers and that going to them is forbidden, even though the Arabs then trusted them.

lessons.title: Keeping a vow and a promise
lessons.body: The ustaz explains that a vow is a promise to Allah and it is a sin not to fulfil it. The Arabs would also never break their promises.

lessons.title: Being kind to your wife and those in your care
lessons.body: Abdullah was kind to his wife Aminah and to the young Ummu Aiman, whom he gave to keep Aminah company.

lessons.title: The Prophet SAW was born into a noble family
lessons.body: Knowing Hashim, Abdul Muttalib and Abdullah helps us understand the family into which the Prophet SAW was born.

glossary.meaning: The Quraysh's two yearly trading journeys: to Sham when Mecca was hot and to Yemen when Mecca was cool.
Crumbling bread into soup. It is from this that Amr was called Hashim.
The old name of Al-Madinah Al-Munawwarah.
An Arab tribe from Yemen who lived in Mecca, later turned wicked and buried zamzam.
An Arab tribe that came to defeat Jurhum and take over Mecca.
A vow or promise to Allah to do something if a request is granted.
Arrows that were drawn to make a decision, as the Arabs did to decide Abdullah's fate.

dalil.context: The ustaz refers to Surah Quraysh, which mentions the winter and summer journeys of the Quraysh.
dalil.translation: secure in their winter and summer journeys.

dalil.context: Allah fed them and kept them safe from hunger and fear, which the ustaz explains as being full and safe.
dalil.translation: who provides them with food to ward off hunger, safety to ward off fear.
The ustaz says that whoever goes to a soothsayer, Allah does not accept his prayer.
dalil.context: Mentioned when the Arabs wanted to ask a soothsayer who owned zamzam. The ustaz does not name a narrator or source.

sirah.era: Before the Prophet's birth: the Prophet's family
sirah.summary: This lecture tells of the Prophet's nearest forebears, Hashim, Abdul Muttalib and Abdullah, up to Abdullah's death while Aminah was carrying him.
